name: SEMIOS Benchmark
description: This work presents an experimental benchmark comparing two information localization strategies in language models: (A) In-Context Learning with full prompts and (B) Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) with short prompts. Using a controlled Structured Entity Extraction (SEE) task on consumer hardware (RTX 3060 12GB), we measure Total Physical Cost (TPC) defined as energy consumed (Joules), latency (seconds), VRAM usage (GB), and accuracy (Exact Match). Results demonstrate that while Baseline B significantly reduces input tokens (-59%), it exhibits higher energy consumption (+21%) and latency (+170%) due to implementation overhead in native Python versus an optimized engine (Ollama). This work contributes a replicable TPC measurement methodology and demonstrates that token reductions do not automatically translate into energy savings, providing parameters for future research on inference efficiency.
